properties.name: A field report cites the version that answered it, and the kit-manifest gate is actually run
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word 2026-08-28, on all three parts. Two landed; the third could not.

⭐ THE INSTRUCTION WAS MANUFACTURING BAD FIELD REPORTS, WHICH IS WHY IT WENT FIRST. A skill reflow2 SERVES told the reporter to cite a file that said 0.11.0 while the server answering was 0.39.0. Alex cross-checked four sources and caught it; a reporter who did not would have filed against a version that was never running. The fix depends on `cap:the-handshake-is-written-down-beside-the-graph`, built hours earlier — which gave the skill an accurate source to point AT rather than only a warning to point AWAY from.

⚠️ VERIFIED, NOT TRUSTED, TWICE. The installer's dry run was read before it was run (11 changes, all `keep`, nothing deleted — it recognises the edited skill mirrors and leaves them). Afterwards the manifest was read OUT OF THE FILE — 0.41.0, d3cb4ab, 36 files — rather than from the installer's own "Now: reflow2 0.41.0" line, because `fact:the-v0380-manifest-shipped-empty-because-a-dry-run-reads-like-a-write` records a dry run reading exactly like a write. The pre-existing failure was confirmed by stashing the tree and re-running: still exit 1 without this session's edits.

🛑 THE CI GATE WAS ADDED, MEASURED AND REVERTED, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL PART. Everything that motivated it was true: the check existed, failed on a clean tree, and ran nowhere. What nobody had checked was whether CI has an installation to check. It does not — `.reflow2/` is gitignored, `git ls-files .reflow2/` is empty, and the check exits 2 on such a tree, so the gate would have turned every build red. The fresh-install case that COULD run there is already covered by `test_init.py`. An `INVALIDATES` claiming the finding closed was drawn and then deleted; `fact:the-kit-manifest-gate-cannot-run-in-ci-because-ci-is-never-installed-into` carries the measurement.

📌 A CANDIDATE THAT WOULD REACH IT, recorded rather than built: the server already writes `reflow2_version` into `<graph>.client.json` and `.reflow2/kit-version.json` sits beside it. Comparing them and saying so — as `served_by.stale` already does for a replaced binary — reaches the developer AND the field without CI being involved at all.

⚠️ NOT FIXED, AND SEPARATE: the RELEASE binary is stale relative to its source, which the installer warned about. A cousin of this staleness, left as its own thing.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Item 3 of the 2026-08-27 field report. `report-friction` told reporters to cite `.reflow2/kit-version.json`; it now says to read `.reflow2/graph.client.json`, the handshake sidecar, which names the reflow2 that actually ANSWERED the session plus the client and negotiated MCP revision. The installer was re-run to clear the drift (0.30.0 → 0.41.0, verified by reading the file). 🛑 THE CI GATE WAS ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED: `check_kit_manifest.py` cannot run in CI because `.reflow2/` is gitignored, so a checkout has no installation and the check exits 2. `fact:defect-kit-manifest-drift-is-invisible-to-ci` is NOT closed — it is sharpened, and the sharpening makes it harder.
